title: Real Numbers - Prove Irrationality
triggers: Prove that sqrt(3) is an irrational number
bypass: Step 1: Assume the number is rational, i.e., equal to p/q where p and q are co-prime integers and q is not zero. Step 2: Square both sides and show that p^2 is a multiple of the prime number, hence p is also a multiple. Step 3: Substitute p and show q^2 is also a multiple. Step 4: This contradicts the co-prime assumption. Hence, irrational.

title: Real Numbers - HCF & LCM Properties
bypass: Formula: HCF x LCM = Product of the two numbers. For prime factorization: HCF = product of the smallest powers of common prime factors. LCM = product of the greatest powers of all prime factors involved. 'Greatest number that divides' means find HCF. 'Smallest number divisible by' means find LCM.

title: Polynomials - Zeroes and Coefficients
triggers: relationship between the zeroes and coefficients
bypass: For quadratic polynomial ax^2 + bx + c: Sum of zeroes (alpha + beta) = -b/a. Product of zeroes (alpha * beta) = c/a. To form a polynomial with given zeroes: x^2 - (Sum of zeroes)x + (Product of zeroes). To find zeroes, split the middle term.

title: Linear Equations - Consistency and Solutions
bypass: Unique solution (Intersecting lines): a1/a2 != b1/b2. Infinitely many solutions (Coincident lines): a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2. No solution (Parallel lines / Inconsistent): a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2. Compare coefficients of the two equations and solve for unknown variable k.

title: Linear Equations - Word Problems
bypass: For fraction: Let numerator be x, denominator y. For two-digit number: Let unit digit be x, tens digit y, Original Number = 10y + x, Reversed = 10x + y. For age: Let present ages be x and y. '5 years ago' = x-5, y-5. '5 years hence' = x+5, y+5. Form two linear equations and solve using substitution or elimination.

title: Quadratic Equations - Nature of Roots
bypass: Calculate Discriminant (D) = b^2 - 4ac. If D > 0: Two distinct real roots. If D = 0: Two equal real roots (x = -b/2a). If D < 0: No real roots. When question says 'has two equal roots', set b^2 - 4ac = 0 and solve for the missing variable.

title: Quadratic Equations - Speed and Distance Word Problems
triggers: train travels at a certain average speed
bypass: Let usual speed be x km/hr. Time = Distance / Speed. Form equation: (Distance/x) - (Distance/(x + speed_increase)) = Time difference. Solve the resulting quadratic equation for x by splitting the middle term or using the quadratic formula. Reject negative speed.

title: Arithmetic Progressions - Finding nth Term
bypass: Formula: a_n = a + (n-1)d. Where 'a' is first term, 'd' is common difference (a2 - a1), 'n' is number of terms. To find the number of terms when last term is given, set a_n = Last term and solve for n. Middle term = (n+1)/2 th term if n is odd.

title: Arithmetic Progressions - Sum of n Terms
triggers: sum of its first n terms
bypass: Formula 1: S_n = n/2 * [2a + (n-1)d]. Formula 2: S_n = n/2 * (a + l) where l is the last term. If a sequence is given as a formula for S_n, find a_n using a_n = S_n - S_(n-1).

title: Coordinate Geometry - Distance Formula & Equidistance
bypass: Distance = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2). If point P(x, y) is equidistant from A and B, then PA^2 = PB^2. 'Point on x-axis' means y=0, coordinates are (x,0). 'Point on y-axis' means x=0, coordinates are (0,y). Equate distances, square both sides to remove roots, and solve.

title: Coordinate Geometry - Section Formula
bypass: Section Formula: P(x, y) = [ (m1*x2 + m2*x1) / (m1+m2) , (m1*y2 + m2*y1) / (m1+m2) ]. Mid-point formula: ((x1+x2)/2 , (y1+y2)/2). If ratio is asked, assume it to be k:1. If divided by x-axis, put y-coordinate of section formula to 0. If y-axis, put x-coordinate to 0.

title: Triangles - Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT/Thales)
triggers: line is drawn parallel to one side
bypass: BPT: If a line is parallel to one side of a triangle intersecting the other two sides, it divides them in the same ratio (AD/DB = AE/EC). Often used with properties of Trapezium (diagonals divide proportionally) or mid-point theorem.
visual_blueprint: Triangle ABC with a line DE drawn parallel to base BC, cutting AB at D and AC at E.

title: Triangles - Similarity Criteria
bypass: Use AA, SAS, or SSS similarity criteria. If Triangle ABC ~ Triangle PQR, then AB/PQ = BC/QR = AC/PR. Also, Ratio of Perimeters = Ratio of corresponding sides = Ratio of corresponding altitudes/medians.

title: Circles - Tangents from External Point
triggers: tangents drawn from an external point
prove that AB + CD = AD + BC
bypass: Theorem: Lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal. For a quadrilateral ABCD circumscribing a circle, use this theorem 4 times from vertices A, B, C, D to the touch points, then add all equations to prove opposite sides sum are equal (AB + CD = AD + BC).
visual_blueprint: Quadrilateral circumscribing a circle with touch points P, Q, R, S marked on the sides.

title: Circles - Radius and Tangent Perpendicularity
triggers: inclined to each other at an angle
bypass: Theorem: Radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact (Angle = 90 degrees). This creates right-angled triangles where you can use Pythagoras theorem or Trigonometry (sin, cos, tan) to find missing lengths (like distance from center) or angles. Angle between tangents + Angle between radii at center = 180 degrees.
visual_blueprint: Circle with center O, external point P, tangents PA and PB. Triangle OAP is a right-angled triangle at A.

title: Trigonometry - T-Ratios and Value Substitution
bypass: Memorize the table for 0, 30, 45, 60, 90 degrees. If sin(A+B) = 1, then A+B = 90. If cos(A-B) = sqrt(3)/2, then A-B = 30. Add/subtract equations to find A and B. For evaluate questions, carefully substitute values and rationalize the denominator if a root is present in the final answer.

title: Trigonometry - Proving Identities
bypass: Step 1: Convert all sec, cosec, tan, cot into sin and cos. Step 2: Take LCM to combine fractions. Step 3: Use core identities: sin^2(x) + cos^2(x) = 1, 1 + tan^2(x) = sec^2(x), 1 + cot^2(x) = cosec^2(x). Step 4: Factorize or use algebraic identities like a^2-b^2 to cancel terms and reach RHS.

title: Heights & Distances - Angles of Elevation & Depression
bypass: Draw the figure accurately: vertical lines for towers/buildings, horizontal for ground. Mark angles. Use tan(theta) = Perpendicular/Base in most cases. For double triangles (e.g., car moving towards tower), apply tan in the smaller right triangle first, then the larger one, and substitute the common side (usually height) to find the distance.
visual_blueprint: Two right-angled triangles sharing a common vertical height, representing the two positions of an object moving towards or away from a tower.

title: Areas Related to Circles - Area of Sector and Arc Length
bypass: Area of Sector = (theta / 360) * pi * r^2. Length of Arc = (theta / 360) * 2 * pi * r. For clock problems: Angle swept by minute hand in 1 minute is 6 degrees. Multiply by given minutes to find theta, then apply sector formula.

title: Areas Related to Circles - Area of Segment and Shaded Regions
bypass: Area of Minor Segment = Area of Sector - Area of Triangle. If angle is 90, Area of Triangle = 1/2 * base * height (r*r). If angle is 60, triangle is equilateral, Area = (sqrt(3)/4) * r^2. Area of Major Segment = Area of Circle - Area of Minor Segment. Shaded region = Outer Shape Area - Inner Unshaded Shape Area.

title: Surface Areas & Volumes - Combination of Solids
triggers: surface area of the remaining solid
tent is in the shape of
bypass: For TSA of combined solids: Add the Curved Surface Areas (CSA) of the visible parts. DO NOT use TSA formulas directly. E.g., Tent (Cylinder + Cone) = CSA of Cylinder + CSA of Cone. Solid with cavity: Area = CSA outer + CSA inner + Area of remaining bases. Slant height l = sqrt(r^2 + h^2).

title: Surface Areas & Volumes - Melting and Recasting
triggers: water is flowing at the rate of
bypass: Principle: Volume remains constant. Volume of original solid = N * Volume of one new solid. To find N, divide total volume by volume of one piece. For water flow: Volume of water = Cross-section Area of pipe * Speed * Time. Equate this to Volume of tank (L * B * H) to find time or height rise.

title: Statistics - Mean and Missing Frequencies
bypass: Direct Method: Mean = Sum(f_i * x_i) / Sum(f_i), where x_i is the class mark (midpoint). Assumed Mean Method: Mean = a + [Sum(f_i * d_i) / Sum(f_i)], where d_i = x_i - a. For missing frequency, substitute the given mean into the formula and solve for the unknown 'f' or 'x'.
visual_blueprint: Five-column Statistics Table: Class Interval, Frequency (f), Class Mark (x), Deviation (d), Product (f*d).

title: Statistics - Median, Mode & Empirical Formula
bypass: Median = L + [((N/2 - cf)/f) * h]. Create cumulative frequency (cf) column. Find N/2 to locate Median Class. Mode = L + [((f1 - f0)/(2f1 - f0 - f2)) * h]. Locate highest frequency for Modal Class. Empirical Formula: 3*Median = Mode + 2*Mean. 'Less than' table gives cf, subtract sequentially to get normal frequencies.

title: Probability - Cards, Dice, and Coins
triggers: drawn from a well shuffled deck
bypass: Probability P(E) = Number of Favorable Outcomes / Total Possible Outcomes. Cards: Total = 52. Face cards = 12 (J, Q, K of 4 suits). Dice: 2 dice total outcomes = 36. Doublets, sum=X are common questions. Coins: 2 coins = 4 outcomes (HH, HT, TH, TT). 'At least one' means 1 or more. P(E) + P(not E) = 1.
